thread:
Evelyn (oncall): getting an alert — 503s spiking for hosted inference in us-west1. Errors: ~18% 503 rate on /v1/generate for model: redwood-ggml-large. Clients reporting timeouts. Digging in now. sup ticket SUP-4239
Alex T: looking at grafana — request latency and 5xx count both up starting ~1836543000. Heap of restarts on node gpu-usw1-23.
Maya P: I see repeated container restarts from the k8s events on that node: CrashLoopBackOff -> OOMKilled -> Restarting.
Chris L: grabbing pod logs now. past 10 lines show CUDA OOM messages then a segfault.
Chris L: ```
[2026-11-02T13:33:10Z] model_server: allocation failed: cannot allocate 1627 MB (GPU 0)
[2026-11-02T13:33:10Z] worker(0): cudaMemcpyAsync: out of memory
[2026-11-02T13:33:10Z] worker(0): Received signal SIGSEGV (segfault)
#0 0x7f8b1c3b in some_kernel + 0x4f
#1 0x7f8b2a2c in worker_loop + 0x1a3
```
Jordana K: infra-bot shows a deploy happened ~30s before spike: deploy id dpl-8721 (model-serving). Any config changes in that deploy?
infra-bot: Deploy dpl-8721 by maya.p at 1836542956 -> rolled out to us-west1. Changes: default_batch_size: 8 -> 16; enable_prefetch: true.
Maya P: yes that was the roll for throughput tuning — increased batch default for that model variant. Didn't expect a memory regression on GPUs but plausible.
Evelyn (oncall): ok immediate mitigation options? We should stop the churn for customer impact.
Alex T: recommended quick actions: 1) scale down replicas on overloaded node, 2) pin traffic away from that node (cordon + drain), 3) pin model traffic to previous variant (roll back dpl-8721).
Rick (support): customer-facing note: informing affected tenants and linking to SUP-4239. ETA for fix?
Chris L: doing a patch: update deployment to set batch_size=4 for redwood-ggml-large on us-west1 and restart pods. Applying now.```
Evelyn (oncall): rolling the change.
infra-bot: Rolling update started for deployment redwood-ggml-large-us-west1 at 1836543360
Maya P: also enabling the fallback route to redwood-ggml-medium for sessions that hit failures. Adding fast-failover in routing policy.
Alex T: running a quick query on error traces to ensure we're not missing related kernel driver faults. So far only pods on kernel image linux-5.17.12 show repeats.
Chris L: more logs after the batch_size change show fewer OOMs but a couple of pods still segfaulting and restarting.
Chris L: ```
[2026-11-02T13:40:22Z] model_server: allocation attempted: 512 MB -> succeeded
[2026-11-02T13:40:23Z] worker(1): processing ok
[2026-11-02T13:40:40Z] worker(2): Received signal SIGABRT - aborting after internal error
[2026-11-02T13:40:40Z] stack: /opt/inference/lib/infer.so(+0x9b12)
```
Jordana K: looking at node metrics — GPU memory fragmentation is high on some nodes. Could be driver + allocation pattern regression.
Evelyn (oncall): support-bot can you enqueue a high-priority incident ticket and notify infra oncall?
support-bot: Created incident INC-2026-11-02-05. Notifying infra-oncall.
Rick (support): customer update sent: "We're investigating increased 503s in us-west1 for model redwood-ggml-large. Mitigations in progress; we'll follow up with a timeline." :thumbsup:
Maya P: long-term we should add a memory-safeguard that rejects batch_size>12 on older kernel/nv driver combos. I'll open a PR.
Alex T: can we confirm if a node-level GPU driver update happened in the last maintenance window?
Jordana K: cluster events show a node reboot 1836542200 with a kernel/driver bump to nvidia-driver 535.12. That correlates with the failing node set.
Chris L: ok hypothesis: driver bump + increased batch_size exposed a memory allocation path that leads to segfault. Repro steps I'm trying locally: set batch=16, run load-test with 2k tokens, watch for OOM then segfault.
Evelyn (oncall): set up temporary routing: move 80% of traffic to us-east1, 20% to us-west1 so customers see degraded but up service.
infra-bot: Traffic routing updated: us-east1=80%, us-west1=20% at 1836543601
Chris L: local repro succeeded — OOM then SIGABRT when batch_size >= 14 on driver 535.12. Not reproducible on 534.x.
Maya P: plan: 1) roll back driver on affected node pool to 534.x (coord with infra SRE), 2) keep batch_size cap in serving config, 3) revert dpl-8721 if rollback not fast.
Evelyn (oncall): I'll coordinate rollback with SRE. Rick please hold customer comms for a more detailed postmortem.
Rick (support): will do. Notifying enterprise contacts and listing mitigations.
Jordana K: started node pool rollback to driver 534.98 on two affected hosts at 1836543720.
infra-bot: Node pool rollback job started: job-rollback-334 at 1836543725
Chris L: after one node rolled back, segfaults stopped on that node; 503 rate trending down.
Evelyn (oncall): good. leaving this thread open until rollback complete and service stable. We'll produce a root-cause doc after investigation (likely driver+batch regression).
Rick (support): SUP-4239 updated with status and note that temporary cap applied and driver rollback in progress.
Maya P: opening a change to prevent future deploys that bump default_batch_size without a canary on kernel mismatches.
Alex T: next steps: postmortem, add mem-safeguard, add canary gating for batch defaults.
Evelyn (oncall): final update: last observed 503 spike cleared at 1836543850. Marking incident as mitigated. We'll reconvene for RCA.
support-bot: Incident INC-2026-11-02-05 status -> mitigated at 1836543855
Rick (support): follow-up scheduled with customers for 11/03 10:00 PT. Closing thread after RCA doc."
